_doc: THE TRODDEN GROUND OF THE FORT'S PARADE (T-3320). The parade's own footprint, laid by renderers/web/js/yards.js as `trodden_earth` and feathered into the sward, in place of the archetype's flat 6 cm slab (which buildings.js leaves out). NOT ONE COORDINATE HERE IS AUTHORED - the ring is derived from data/sidecars/1812/first_fort_dearborn_parade.json by tools/generate_fort_parade_ground.py and tools/check.sh re-derives this file byte for byte. IT DRAWS NO FENCE (`runs: []`). Every value is `reconstructed`; docs/LIBERTIES.md L-t3320-parade-ground states what bounds it.
name: The trodden ground of the first Fort Dearborn's parade
coordinates: Local East-North-Up metres from data/datum.json's origin - the frame the sidecars' placement.local_e / local_n use.

derived_from.note: The parade's footprint and placement are the record's (inferred); this ground inherits them and adds only a reconstructed surface and its feather.

existence.note: That the parade was open ground is the parade record's; that it was bare, trodden earth fading raggedly into grass at its edges is this project's reading of a garrison's drill ground. docs/LIBERTIES.md L-t3320-parade-ground.

runs_note: EMPTY, AND DELIBERATELY. The parade is open ground between the fort's own buildings; there is no fence for this record to draw.

ground.note: The apron's treatment (fort_dearborn_apron, L174): finer and darker than a wagon yard, without ruts, so the fort's ground reads as one surface inside and outside its walls.
ground.fringe_note: The sward feathers in from the parade's own edge over 5.0 m, a wandering ragged fade rather than a line - the owner's ask.

assertions.claim: the parade ring pushed out 5.0 m on every side stands inside first_fort_dearborn_pickets_inner's footprint, so the fade never reaches the pickets or the ground outside them
no other enclosure record in this scene already lays an area treatment on the parade (a door's road_earth path may run onto it)

research_note: WHAT WOULD MOVE THIS OFF RECONSTRUCTION: a garrison description, return or drawing that shows the parade's surface - grass, gravel or bare earth.
